TASK: act as a librarian. Research how web applications can present an uploaded PowerPoint (.pptx/.ppt) file with FULL fidelity - meaning user-specified fonts, entrance/exit animations, slide transitions, embedded images, and embedded video/audio all actually play, not a flattened static image.

DELIVERABLE: A comparison table of every viable technical approach, each with: what it preserves (fonts / build animations / transitions / video / audio / interactivity), what it loses, licensing or cost requirements, and whether it can run self-hosted. Include at minimum: (a) LibreOffice headless / Gotenberg / unoconv conversion to PDF or images, (b) Microsoft 365 / Office Online / PowerPoint for the web embedding via Microsoft Graph or OneDrive/SharePoint embed URLs, (c) Aspose.Slides and Nutrient/PSPDFKit and other commercial SDKs, (d) open-source JS renderers such as PPTXjs / js-pptx / docxjs, (e) PPTX -> MP4 video export via PowerPoint automation or LibreOffice, (f) capturing the presenter's own real PowerPoint app via WebRTC getDisplayMedia screen sharing. For each, cite official documentation with URLs.

SCOPE: External documentation and vendor docs only. Do NOT read or edit any repository files. Read-only analysis; return findings as text.

VERIFY: For each claim about what a tool preserves or drops, cite the specific official doc page. Explicitly state where documentation is silent rather than guessing. Pay special attention to documented statements about whether LibreOffice conversion preserves PowerPoint animations and transitions, and whether Office Online embeds support animation playback.

STOP WHEN: The comparison table is complete with citations for every row.

# Presenting uploaded PowerPoint files with full fidelity in a web app — approach comparison

**Research date:** 2026-08-15 · Sources: vendor/official documentation only (Microsoft Support/Learn, TDF/LibreOffice, Gotenberg, Aspose, Nutrient/PSPDFKit, ONLYOFFICE, MDN, project repos/npm registry). Where a doc is silent, the cell says **"docs silent"** — nothing below is inferred from blog posts or forum threads.

## Bottom line (before the table)

No single path preserves *everything* interactively. Two approaches are genuinely "the real thing": **(b) embed actual PowerPoint** (PowerPoint for the web iframe from OneDrive/SharePoint) and **(f) capture the real desktop app** via `getDisplayMedia`. Everything else converts: PDF/images (a) flatten animations and media; Aspose HTML5 (c) replays animations/transitions as JavaScript but with a documented *unsupported-effects* list and unverified media handling; open-source JS renderers (d) don't do PowerPoint animations at all; MP4 export (e) is a video, not an interactive presentation.

## The comparison

| Approach | Preserves | Loses | Licensing / cost | Self-hosted? | Official-doc citations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **(a) LibreOffice headless / Gotenberg / unoconv → PDF or images** | Slide layout, text, embedded images, fonts *mostly* (substitution caveat); slide **transitions can be carried into PDF** as viewer preferences (`useTransitionEffects`); notes/hidden slides exportable | **No build animations** (no animation export option exists; LibreOffice docs never mention animation preservation); embedded **video/audio playback in the export: docs silent** (not exported as media in PDF); macros disabled; "not a 1:1 clone of Microsoft Office… complex styling, SmartArt… may render slightly differently"; missing fonts = layout shift | Free. LibreOffice: open source, no fee; Gotenberg MIT; unoconv GPL-2.0, **archived**, README says deprecated → Unoserver | **Yes** — Docker-friendly, fully offline | Gotenberg "Convert with LibreOffice → PDF" (fonts/macros/`useTransitionEffects`/`exportNotes`/`exportHiddenSlides`); github.com/unoconv/unoconv (README); github.com/gotenberg/gotenberg (MIT) |
| **(b) PowerPoint for the web embed (M365 / OneDrive / SharePoint iframe; Graph for access)** | **Everything PowerPoint itself can play in its web renderer**: slide animations ("Playing slide animations ●"), transitions (editing "Limited" but playback supported), **audio & video playback in slide show ●**, YouTube videos ●; embedded images/SmartArt display; edits to the OneDrive file auto-reflect in the embed | Web platform gaps (official table): **can't add audio**, can't trim/bookmark/fade audio or video, **animation triggers ✕**, "adding, removing, and changing" animations/transitions only "Limited", no self-running presentations / Presenter View / recording, can't add charts, SmartArt "Limited" | Microsoft 365 subscription; requires hosting files in OneDrive/SharePoint; anonymous-viewer auth requirements: **docs silent** | **No** — Microsoft-hosted only | support.microsoft.com "Embed a presentation in a web page or blog"; support.microsoft.com "Compare PowerPoint features on different platforms" (audio/slide/video/slide-show tables); Microsoft docs on a *headless* server-side render API: **silent** |
| **(c) Aspose.Slides (commercial SDK)** | HTML5 export: **animations and transitions replayed in-browser** (`AnimateShapes`, `AnimateTransitions`, generated `animation.js`/`effects.js`); PDF export: layout/formatting preserved; video export: `PresentationAnimationsGenerator` + `PresentationPlayer` + ffmpeg | Documented **unsupported effects** (e.g., Appear entrance ✕, Pulse emphasis ✕, Morph and several "Exciting" transitions ✕); PDF export: font substitution possible, animations unmentioned; **media playback in HTML5 output: docs silent**; evaluation watermark | Commercial — perpetual per-developer license, offline validation (docs.aspose.com/slides/net/licensing); exact pricing not on docs pages | **Yes** — on-prem SDK (.NET/Java/Python etc.), ffmpeg needed for video export | docs.aspose.com/slides/net/export-to-html5/ · /convert-powerpoint-to-video/ · /convert-powerpoint-to-pdf/ · /licensing/ |
| **(c′) Nutrient (PSPDFKit) JS Office viewer** | Browser viewer for Word/Excel/**PPT** (product page title: "JavaScript Office viewer: Word, Excel, PPT \| Nutrient"); page advertises a Markdown doc variant | **Fidelity claims (native vs. rasterized slides, animations, transitions, media playback) could not be extracted** — pspdfkit.com unreachable from this environment and Wayback has no capture of the guide; flagged **unverified**, do not take on faith | Commercial (paid licensing); terms not verified this session | **Yes** — self-hosted JS SDK (per product positioning; license terms unverified) | pspdfkit.com/guides/web/office/ (title confirmed; content unreadable this session) |
| **(d) Open-source JS renderers** | **PPTXjs**: text, fonts, pictures, video (HTML5 player), audio, charts, SmartArt, tables, themes; its own `slideMode` synthesizes simple transitions | **No PowerPoint animations** — absent from the feature list; open issue #6 "Any plan to support animations?" (open since 2021); font fidelity of extracted text: docs silent; project last pushed 2022 | Free. PPTXjs MIT; **js-pptx**: GPL per README (GitHub metadata: "Other"), abandoned since 2015, "cannot yet… generate themes, layouts, masters, animations"; **docx** (docxjs): MIT but it is a **.docx generator**, not a PPTX renderer (npm description: "Easily generate .docx files…") | **Yes** — client-side | github.com/meshesha/PPTXjs (+ issues/6); github.com/won21kr/js-pptx; npmjs.com/package/docx (registry metadata) |
| **(e) PPTX → MP4 (PowerPoint automation or LibreOffice)** | **Real PowerPoint export**: "You can include animations and transitions in your movie"; embedded video "will play correctly"; scriptable via VBA `Presentation.CreateVideo(FileName, UseTimingsAndNarrations, DefaultSlideDuration, VertResolution, FramesPerSecond, Quality)` — server automation possible in principle | **It's a video, not an interactive deck**; official drops: linked media, QuickTime media, macros, OLE/ActiveX; requires Windows + Office per conversion; **Office EULA terms for unattended server automation: not verified this session** (commonly restricted — check licensing) · **LibreOffice→MP4: docs silent** — TDF wiki search "mp4 export" returns 0 hits; no documented export | Office license cost; output is free | Partially — needs Windows+Office (or undocumented LO+ffmpeg glue) | support.microsoft.com "Turn your presentation into a video"; OfficeDev/VBA-content repo (PowerPoint `Presentation.CreateVideo`); TDF wiki: **0 hits on "mp4 export"** (documented silence) |
| **(f) WebRTC `getDisplayMedia` capture of the real PowerPoint app** | **Pixel-exact fidelity by construction** — the real app plays fonts, animations, transitions, video, audio (`audio: true` in the constraint), interactivity; stream recordable (MediaRecorder) or sent live over WebRTC | **No viewer interactivity** — someone must run the slideshow (or a driver must click); user-consent prompt required on the capturing machine; encoding is lossy; DRM'd/blocked content behavior: docs silent; one PowerPoint instance per stream | Free (browser API); PowerPoint license for the presenting machine | **Yes** — purely client-side | developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getDisplayMedia |
| *(optional)* **ONLYOFFICE Docs + Conversion API** | Self-hosted editor renders/edits PPTX in-browser; Conversion API converts pptx → pdf, pdfa, png, jpg, gif, bmp, odp, otp, pot/potx/pptm/ppsx/potm (official conversion tables) | **No HTML output and no video output for PPTX** in the tables; fidelity of animations/transitions/media through conversion: **docs silent**; editor playback of animations: docs silent (a 9.4 release banner mentions "new slide themes & transitions" for the *editor*, not conversion) | Free open-source Community edition; paid commercial editions (not re-verified) | **Yes** — server component | api.onlyoffice.com/docs/docs-api/additional-api/conversion-api/ (+ /conversion-tables/) |

## Notes per approach (evidence trail)

**(a)** Gotenberg's LibreOffice module (renamed from "LibreOffice module" to "Convert with LibreOffice → PDF") explicitly warns: *"not a 1:1 clone of Microsoft Office… complex styling, SmartArt… may render slightly differently"* and *"Missing fonts are the most common cause of layout issues"*; macros are disabled. Its PDF options include `exportNotes`, `exportHiddenSlides`, and `useTransitionEffects` ("use transition effects when advancing slides") — but **no animation-export option exists**, and the TDF help/wiki returns zero results for both "pdf export animations" and "mp4 export". unoconv's README confirms it converts any LO-importable to any LO-exportable format but is deprecated in favor of Unoserver; the repo is archived (last push 2023).

**(b)** Microsoft's official embed article: iframe code is obtained from PowerPoint for the web/OneDrive, and updates to the source file auto-reflect in the embed. The "Compare PowerPoint features on different platforms" table (fetched in full) gives the web column: *Playing slide animations ●*, *Playing audio ● / Playing in slide show ● / Playing across slides ●*, *Playing other video types ●*, *Playing YouTube videos ●*, *Adding audio ◌*, *Trimming, bookmarking, and fading ◌*, *Animation triggers ◌*, transitions/animation *editing* "Limited", *Self-running presentation ◌*. Microsoft documents **no headless API** that renders PPTX with animations server-side — that is a documented-silence gap.

**(c)** Aspose HTML5 export is the only captured commercial path that explicitly documents in-browser animation/transition replay (options `AnimateShapes` / `AnimateTransitions`, generated `animation.js` + `effects.js` with jQuery/Anime.js), but the same docs carry support matrices excluding effects (Appear entrance, Pulse emphasis, Morph, several "Exciting" transitions). PDF conversion docs mention font substitution and layout preservation but not animations. Licensing page: perpetual per-developer, offline validation, evaluation watermark. Nutrient/PSPDFKit's guide page title is confirmed (rebrand to Nutrient) but its content was not retrievable this session — **its fidelity claims remain unverified here**.

**(d)** PPTXjs README lists text/fonts/pictures/video/audio/charts/SmartArt/tables/themes but **no PowerPoint animations**; GitHub issue #6 ("Any plan to support animations?") has been open since 2021; last push 2022. js-pptx is explicitly early-stage ("cannot yet… generate themes, layouts, masters, animations, etc.") and abandoned since 2015. docx is a Word-document generator (npm description verbatim) — included only to rule it out.

**(e)** Microsoft's article is explicit that animations/transitions are baked into the exported movie and embedded video plays correctly, while linked media, QuickTime media, macros, and OLE/ActiveX objects are dropped. `Presentation.CreateVideo` (VBA) makes it scriptable. LibreOffice has **no documented** MP4 export (TDF wiki search = 0 hits).

**(f)** MDN documents the user-prompt, display/window/tab selection, `audio: true` for audio capture, and that the stream can be recorded (MediaStream Recording API) or sent over WebRTC — i.e., the exact fidelity of the source app, at the cost of live interactivity and a running desktop instance.

## Remaining uncertainty (explicit)

1. **Nutrient/PSPDFKit**: page title and existence verified; animation/transition/media fidelity, raster-vs-native rendering, and pricing **not verified** — do not treat as a fidelity claim until their guide is read.
2. **PowerPoint-for-the-web fonts**: Microsoft's tables cover animation/audio/video but say nothing about font-substitution behavior in the browser renderer — **docs silent**.
3. **PowerPoint automation licensing**: unattended/server-side Office automation is subject to Microsoft licensing terms that this research did not verify (Microsoft docs are silent in the pages captured).
4. **Media in Aspose HTML5 output** and **media in LibreOffice PDF output**: neither vendor documents playback of embedded video/audio in those outputs — **docs silent**.
5. **LibreOffice license metadata**: GitHub's API detection for LibreOffice/core reports GPL-3.0; the TDF license page 301/404'd on fetch, so the commonly cited MPL-2.0 statement was not re-verified — treat as "free/open source" without an SPDX claim.
6. **Google Slides** was investigated but support.google.com was unreachable from this environment — excluded; its embed/convert behavior is not covered above.

## Recommendation

If the requirement is *interactive, full-fidelity playback in a web app*, only **(b)** (M365/OneDrive embed — if Microsoft hosting is acceptable) or **(f)** (getDisplayMedia of a real PowerPoint instance — if a desktop seat per stream is acceptable) delivers it today, and only (f) is self-hosted. If a *replayed, non-interactive* experience is acceptable, **(e)** (PowerPoint → MP4) is the highest-fidelity documented path, with **(c)** Aspose HTML5 as the only documented self-hosted interactive-replay option — budget for its unsupported-effect list and verify media handling with a test deck before committing. **(a)/(d)** are cheap but flatten animations and media, so they only satisfy "full fidelity" if your definition excludes build animations entirely.
